title: Pi tool registration
responsibility: Expose the existing typed libraries to the agent as validated Pi tools and nothing more: project status and lint reads, artifact creation and mutation through the existing registries, project-type activation, stage attestation reads and writes, the research and validation capability adapters, and delegation. Own the tool schemas and result rendering; leave every business rule in `lib/`. Launch the session with Pi's built-in filesystem and shell mutation tools disabled.
notes: ⚠️ DISABLING THE BUILT-INS IS THE POINT, NOT AN OPTIMISATION. Pi's default active set includes bash, write and edit — measured, not assumed. An orchestrator holding those can write planning content around the locked, validated, atomic path that decision #88 makes the only legal one, and it will, because editing a file is easier than calling a typed tool. ⚠️ THE WIRE NAMES ARE FIXED HERE, BECAUSE A TOOL NAME IS A CONTRACT. A model is told them, a specialist allowlist names them, and the package's signature declares them - three places that must agree, so they are not improvised per wrapper. TSK-0044 registers exactly these 22: kiln_create_requirement, kiln_create_assertion, kiln_create_evidence, kiln_create_runbook_step, kiln_create_question, kiln_create_decision, kiln_create_component, kiln_create_acceptance_criterion, kiln_create_task, kiln_link_evidence, kiln_unlink_evidence, kiln_revise_artifact, kiln_set_lifecycle, kiln_resolve_question, kiln_link_trace, kiln_unlink_trace, kiln_set_review_status, kiln_set_type_activation, kiln_project_status, kiln_lint, kiln_read_stage_attestations, kiln_write_stage_attestation. ⚠️ WHAT TSK-0044 DOES NOT OWN. TSK-0045 registers its own separately named research, validation and delegation adapters and `kiln_capability`; `kiln_preflight` is TSK-0041's and is setup-only, removed from the effective set before the user-facing session starts, so it must never appear in the orchestrator's measured registry. ⚠️ THE ORDER THE WORK GOES IN, AND WHY. First the signature declares the names, then a check compares that declaration against what registration actually produces - by calling the registration function with a recording stub, the way the package's own test already proves it registers nothing. Without that check the declared `tools` list is the one part of the signature nothing verifies, because tools are not files on disk. Then the read wrappers, then the mutation and attestation wrappers, then the launch flags that disable Pi's built-ins, and last the real-session measurement ACC-0064 asks for - which needs a session against a loopback provider, since no CLI flag lists the active tools and exits.
